chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-ʿUbaydī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say: “Indeed, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, when he intended to relieve himself, would stand at the door of the place and then turn right and left toward his two angels and say: ‘Move away from me; for you two I owe before Allah that I shall not produce any act until I come out to you both.’”

key_terms.أُحْدِثَ حَدَثًا: to produce an act of relieving oneself
key_terms.بَابِ الْمَذْهَبِ: the entrance to the place designated for relieving oneself
key_terms.قَضَاءَ الْحَاجَةِ: relieving oneself; attending to bodily need
key_terms.مَلَكَيْهِ: his two angels, understood as the accompanying recording angels

ai.seo_question: What did Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام say to the two angels when going to relieve himself?
ai.summary: This hadith describes an etiquette observed by Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام when going to relieve himself. It highlights modesty, awareness of the recording angels, and careful conduct in matters connected to ritual purity.
